content:
incident-bot: pager fired -> PD #SEV2: multiple ALB target groups unhealthy in apac1 (auto-escalate in 2m) :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Incident 2026-03-15T02:13:20Z assigned to oncall: Maya Chen (pagerduty runbook attached)
Maya Chen: ack'd. I'm on it, pulling up dashboards.
Maya Chen: quick summary from console: spike in 5xx and TLS handshake errors from edge ALBs to backend pool in apac1, ~40% target unhealthy
Jamal Ortiz: saw alerts for backend-apps as well, looks correlated with a config rollout at 02:05 UTC?
Sasha Ilyas: confirm — we rolled a new nginx sidecar config to the dedicated pool at 02:03 for keepalive tweaks.
Maya Chen: copying runbook steps now. first step: verify ALB target health and TLS error logs.
Maya Chen: running `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...apac1`
Maya Chen: output shows many `target:port` UNHEALTHY with reason `TLS alert handshake failure`
Maya Chen: curling edge from outside to reproduce:
```
curl -v https://edge.apac.redwood.ai/health
* Connected to edge.apac.redwood.ai (13.56.78.90) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Encrypted Extensions (8):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, unknown CA (something something)
* curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert certificate unknown
```
Maya Chen: error looks like cert mismatch or SNI not being forwarded to backend.
Elena Gomez: customer reports starting at ~02:08, increased 502/504s to some tenants in APAC. Support queue getting inbound.
Tom Rivers: can we confirm if the recent sidecar change touched SNI or TLS passthrough?
Sasha Ilyas: sidecar change toggles `proxy_protocol` and reorders cert selection logic — could be related, I flagged it but rollout passed smoke on canaries.
Ryan Patel: I'm going to pause the rollout and revert the sidecar config on the dedicated pool. Jamal, can you prepare a weight shift?
Jamal Ortiz: on it. Preparing ALB weight shift to eu-prod and us-west fallback for traffic from apac1.
Maya Chen: incremental mitigation: mark unhealthy targets OutOfService to force ALB to stop routing (quick fix) while we shift weights.
Jamal Ortiz: running command: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false` then updating weights via route53 / traffic policy.
Maya Chen: checking Route53 for apac edge record TTLs — TTL is 60s, so weight shift should propagate quickly.
Sasha Ilyas: I can also push a hotfix to sidecar to re-enable previous cert selection code, then gradually re-add targets.
Elena Gomez: posting interim message to status page: "Partial edge connectivity issue impacting APAC customers — mitigation in progress." Will update with timeline once stable. :writing_hand:
pagerduty-bot: acknowledged by Maya Chen (03:00 elapsed). Escalation paused.
Ryan Patel: weight shift to eu-prod in progress, monitoring latency and 5xxs...
Maya Chen: after taking unhealthy targets out, backend 5xx rate dropped ~70% but overall customer traffic served via fallback region now.
Jamal Ortiz: weight shift complete at 6210000600, Route53 metrics show 85% traffic moved from apac1 to eu-prod.
Maya Chen: Sasha has a hotfix PR ready. recommend rollback of sidecar to previous config and then re-add targets.
Sasha Ilyas: deploying rollback to dedicated pool now (step 1 of 2).
Maya Chen: after rollback, I'm re-registering targets and checking ALB health checks.
Maya Chen: health checks pass for ~90% of targets after re-register, TLS handshakes normalized on those instances.
Elena Gomez: customer-facing update: "Traffic restored for most customers; APAC serving via fallback while we validate fixes. Full restoration expected within 30 min."
Tom Rivers: capturing timeline for postmortem: config rollout -> 02:03, first PD at 02:13, weight-shift complete 02:23, rollback 02:30, full recovery 02:33 (approx).
Maya Chen: handoff note for next on-call (Ryan): watch for flapping as we reintroduce traffic to apac1. If targets go unhealthy again escalate to SE (SRE lead).
Ryan Patel: ack handoff. I'll stay on for next 45m to watch metrics and DNS rebalance.
pagerduty-bot: incident resolved (status: mitigated) by Maya Chen at 6210001200.
Maya Chen: closing notes: root cause appears to be unintended TLS selection change in sidecar config; canaries missed it due to limited TLS permutations. Action items:
- Revisit canary matrix to include TLS permutations and cert scenarios.
- Add automated synthetic TLS handshake checks to health probes.
- Postmortem w/ timeline and corrective actions, assign owners (Sasha for rollout guardrails, Jamal for routing playbooks).
Elena Gomez: I'll coordinate customer comms and attach impacted tenant list to the postmortem.
Maya Chen: thanks all. I'll file the postmortem and link here when ready. :white_check_mark:
